To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a significant fraction (about 30%) of pages on the Web is created using existing content.
the Web is a large collection of pages that can be classified into four main components: unique pages, copies, copies of copies, and pages that have been removed.

(i) 10% of the Web is composed of pages that are copies of already existing content; (ii) these pages are more frequently returned in the results of real queries and more clicked; and (iii) the sources of the copies are more frequently relevant to the queries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of textual Web content and the relation between sources of content and search engine results.
the analysis of the evolution of textual Web content, the characterization of Web genealogies, and the identification of the sources of Web genealogial trees.
understanding the evolution of the Web, with a special emphasis on the textual content.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evolution of the Web is not a random process, but a process that is strongly influenced by search engine queries.
the Web has evolved from a Web of documents into a Web of documents and copies.
search engines are the most important source of copies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Web is a complex and dynamic environment, where content is created, modified and copied in different forms, and where the same content can be found in different places.
the Web is becoming a huge collection of copies of already existing content.
search engines have an important role in the creation of the Web, and that they have a strong impact on the evolution of the Web content.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Web genealogical trees provide a new perspective for studying the Web evolution, which is complementary to the one provided by traditional Web crawlers.
the Web is a complex ecosystem where content is continuously created from existing content, and where search engines play a key role as sources of content.
the Web is a complex ecosystem, where the creation of new documents is influenced by existing documents, and where the popularity of documents is influenced by the presence of their copies.
